attempts.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) as a router between two previously-unconfigured L2 segments (lan-a on vtnet1/opt1, lan-b on vtnet2/opt2), with static addressing on node2 (10.50.10.11) and node3 (10.50.20.12). Added a manual/hybrid outbound NAT rule scoped to source 10.50.10.0/24 egressing on opt2, so node2→node3 connections arrive at node3 SNAT'd to node1's lan-b address (10.50.20.1), while node3→node2 connections retain node3's real source address (verified via tcpdump on node1's opt2/opt1 interfaces and by observing the peer's addr on each side). Completed the mandatory sequential single-node-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes (node1 via `shutdown -r now`, node2/node3 via `reboot`), confirming boot-identity change on each (FreeBSD kern.boottime; Linux boot_id) and re-verifying post-restart that OPNsense's interface/NAT config persisted from config.xml and that the asymmetric-NAT behavior still functions end-to-end after all three restarts.
